rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report describes the reader using an unordered surah sequence, apparently before Uthman sent standard codices to the provinces and required their order.
rows.anchor: إلى الآفاق بالمصاحف الأئمة المؤلفة على هذا الترتيب المشهور اليوم

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha told him that beginning with any surah would not harm him, and said the first revelation containing Paradise and Hell could be started later in the codex.
rows.anchor: لا يضرك بأي سورة بدأت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Aisha did not mean Surat Iqra by the first surah mentioning Paradise and Hell, Ibn Kathir allows that she meant the category of Mufassal surahs with promise and warning.
rows.anchor: فقد يحتمل أنها أرادت اسم جنس لسور المفصل التي فيها الوعد والوعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir explains that people first embraced faith, then received commands and prohibitions gradually, as an act of divine wisdom and mercy.
rows.anchor: ثم لما انقاد الناس إلى التصديق أمروا ونهوا بالتدريج أولا فأولا وهذا من حكمة الله ورحمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Surah order could be changed, but the arrangement of verses within each surah is fixed by the Prophet; Aisha therefore dictated her written surah verses instead of permitting changes.
rows.anchor: أمر توقيفي عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A sound report from Hudhayfa and Ibn Masud says the Prophet recited al-Baqara, al-Nisa, then Al Imran in night prayer, supporting flexible surah order.
rows.anchor: حديث حذيفة وابن مسعود، وهو في الصحيح أنه، عليه السلام، قرأ في قيام الليل بالبقرة ثم النساء

rows.speaker: أبو بكر بن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbari argues that delaying an earlier surah or advancing a later one is like corrupting the arrangement of verses and letters.
rows.anchor: عن أبي بكر بن الأنباري في كتاب الرد أنه قال: فمن أخر سورة مقدمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir says the familiar surah order in the Uthmanic codex appears partly to reflect Uthman's judgment.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن ترتيب السور فيه منه ما هو رجع إلى رأي عثمان

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir points to Ibn Abbas's question to Uthman about omitting the basmala before Bara'a and classing al-Anfal among the long surahs as evidence of Uthman's judgment; he calls the report's chain good and strong.
rows.anchor: سؤال ابن عباس له في ترك البسملة في أول براءة، وذكره الأنفال من الطول

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir reports that Ali had resolved to arrange the Quran according to its order of revelation.
rows.anchor: وقد ذكرنا عن علي أنه كان قد عزم على ترتيب القرآن بحسب نزوله

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Jundub reports the Prophet warning against explaining the Quran by personal opinion; al-Tirmidhi calls this report gharīb and notes that some scholars criticized Suhayl.
rows.anchor: عن جندب؛ أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

rows.speaker: الترمذي
rows.claim: A version says even an interpretation that happens to be right is still an error; al-Tirmidhi, Abu Dawud, and al-Nasa'i transmit this wording from Suhayl ibn Abi Hazm.
rows.anchor: وقد روى هذا الحديث أبو داود، والترمذي، والنسائي من حديث سهيل بن أبي حزم القطعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir says a person who reaches the right meaning by unsupported opinion still errs by speaking without knowledge and using an unauthorized method; this is less blameworthy than reaching a wrong ruling.
rows.anchor: قد تكلف ما لا علم له به، وسلك غير ما أمر به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He compares this principle to Quran 24:13: accusers are called liars for speaking without witnesses, even if their accusation happened to be true.
rows.anchor: فإذ لم يأتوا بالشهداء فأولئك عند الله هم الكاذبون

rows.speaker: أبو بكر الصديق
rows.claim: Abu Bakr said he would have no refuge on earth or in heaven if he said about God's Book what he did not know, illustrating the early scholars' caution.
rows.anchor: قال أبو بكر الصديق، رضي الله عنه: أي أرض تقلني وأي سماء تظلني؟

rows.speaker: هشام بن محمد بن السائب الكلبي
rows.claim: Hisham al-Kalbi and others say Bishr ibn Abd al-Malik learned writing at al-Anbar, then brought it to Mecca; Harb ibn Umayya and his son Sufyan taught him, Umar learned from Harb, and Muawiya from Sufyan.
rows.anchor: بشر بن عبد الملك أكيدر دومة تعلم الخط من الأنبار، ثم قدم مكة فتزوج الصهباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative account says the first to learn writing from al-Anbar were people of Tayy from Baqqa, who refined and spread it through Arabia.
rows.anchor: إن أول من تعلمه من الأنبار قوم من طيئ من قرية هناك يقال لها: بقة

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Sha'bi says the Muhajirun learned writing from the people of Hira, who in turn learned it from al-Anbar.
rows.anchor: عن الشعبي قال: سألنا المهاجرين من أين تعلمتم الكتابة؟ قالوا: من أهل الحيرة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common early script was al-maktufa; Abu Ali Muqla systematized it and Ibn al-Bawwab further refined it, after which people followed their style.
rows.anchor: والذي كان يغلب على زمان السلف الكتابة المكتوفة ثم هذبها أبو علي مقلة الوزير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn al-Bawwab improved Muqla's writing method, which Ibn Kathir describes as clear and good.
rows.anchor: ثم قربها علي بن هلال البغدادي المعروف بابن البواب وسلك الناس وراءه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because writing was not yet well developed, differences in Quran codices concerned the placement of words as a matter of orthographic craft, not meaning.
rows.anchor: وقع في كتابة المصاحف اختلاف في وضع الكلمات من حيث صناعة الكتابة لا من حيث المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Ubayd and Ibn Abi Dawud wrote and organized material on the orthography of the Quran.
rows.anchor: واعتنى بذلك الإمام الكبير أبو عبيد القاسم بن سلام، رحمه الله، في كتابه فضائل القرآن

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik held that Quran codices should be written only according to the orthography of the authoritative codex, while others allowed different spellings.
rows.anchor: ولهذا نص الإمام مالك، رحمه الله، على أنه لا توضع المصاحف إلا على وضع كتابة الإمام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scholars differed over adding vowel marks and dots to codices, with some permitting and others prohibiting them.
rows.anchor: اختلفوا في الشكل والنقط فمن مرخص ومن مانع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although surah labels, verse markers, tenth divisions, juz, and hizb are common in contemporary codices, Ibn Kathir says following the early generations is preferable.
rows.anchor: فأما كتابة السور وآياتها والتعشير والأجزاء والأحزاب فكثير (3) في مصاحف زماننا، والأولى اتباع السلف الصالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two hadiths describe the Quran's companion as being in a blessed, enviable state; one should wish for the same blessing and congratulate him.
rows.anchor: ومضمون هذين الحديثين: أن صاحب القرآن في غبطة وهو حسن الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghibta means wishing for another's blessing without its removal; condemned envy wishes the blessing removed, whether or not the envier gets it, and was Iblis's first sin against Adam.
rows.anchor: وهذا بخلاف الحسد المذموم وهو تمني زوال نعمة المحسود عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The praiseworthy form of hasad is wishing for the same good state, not its loss to someone else.
rows.anchor: والحسد الشرعي الممدوح هو تمني مثل حال ذلك الذي هو على حالة سارة

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet's statement that there is no hasad except in two cases refers to the Quran reader's private blessing and the charitable spender's benefit to others; Ibn Kathir links it to 35:29.
rows.anchor: قال عليه السلام: "لا حسد إلا في اثنتين "، فذكر النعمة القاصرة وهي تلاوة القرآن

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Yazid ibn al-Akhnas reports the Prophet saying that competition should be limited to a person devoted to the Quran and a person who gives away wealth in charity.
rows.anchor: عن يزيد بن الأخنس، أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "لا تنافس بينكم إلا في اثنتين

rows.speaker: أبو كبشة
rows.claim: Abu Kabsha reports the Prophet dividing people into four: learned and charitable wealth is best; knowledge without wealth earns equal reward when the person intends good; ignorant wealth is squandered; and the poor ignorant person's corrupt wish carries equal burden.
rows.anchor: عن أبي سعيد البختري الطائي، عن أبي كبشة قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول:

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud called Ibn Abbas an excellent interpreter of the Quran; Ibn Kathir says the report's chain to Ibn Masud is sound.
rows.anchor: فهذا إسناد صحيح إلى ابن مسعود: أنه قال عن ابن عباس هذه العبارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas outlived Ibn Masud by thirty-six years, so Ibn Kathir asks the reader to consider how much knowledge he gained afterward.
rows.anchor: وقد مات ابن مسعود، رضي الله عنه، في سنة اثنتين وثلاثين على الصحيح، وعمر بعده ابن عباس ستا وثلاثين سنة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: After Ali appointed him to lead the pilgrimage, Ibn Abbas preached and explained al-Baqara, or al-Nur in another version, so powerfully that Romans, Turks, and Daylamites would have converted if they heard him.
rows.anchor: وقال الأعمش عن أبي وائل: استخلف علي عبد الله بن عباس على الموسم، فخطب الناس، فقرأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Suddi's tafsir mostly transmits from Ibn Masud and Ibn Abbas; sometimes their reports include Israelite material, which the Prophet permitted narrating so long as no one lies about him.
rows.anchor: ولهذا غالب ما يرويه إسماعيل بن عبد الرحمن السدي الكبير في تفسيره، عن هذين الرجلين: عبد الله بن مسعود وابن عباس

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
rows.claim: Ibn Amr acquired two bundles of People of the Book's writings at Yarmuk and narrated from them, relying on the Prophet's permission to relate Israelite reports.
rows.anchor: ولهذا كان عبد الله بن عمرو يوم اليرموك قد أصاب زاملتين من كتب أهل الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir divides Israelite reports into three classes; the first is confirmed by Islamic evidence and is true, while the second is contradicted by Islamic evidence and is false.
rows.anchor: أحدها: ما علمنا صحته مما بأيدينا مما يشهد له بالصدق، فذاك صحيح

rows.speaker: أبو النصر إسماعيل بن حماد الجوهري
rows.claim: Al-Jawhari defines ʿasab as palm frond material above the crown that has not grown leaflets; leaf-bearing material is called saʿaf.
rows.anchor: قال أبو النصر إسماعيل بن حماد الجوهري: وهو من السعف فويق الكرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Likhaf are thin, flat pieces of stone on which the companions wrote Quran, alongside palm stems and other available materials.
rows.anchor: واللخاف: جمع لخفة وهي القطعة من الحجارة مستدقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zayd ibn Thabit gathered Quran from written palm stems, stone pieces, and memorization, because the companions carefully safeguarded the trust entrusted by the Prophet.
rows.anchor: فتلقاه زيد بن ثابت من هذا من عسيبه، ومن هذا من لخافه، ومن صدر هذا، أي من حفظه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir connects the companions' trust in conveying revelation to God's command that the Messenger deliver what was sent down to him.
rows.anchor: ياأيها الرسول بلغ ما أنزل إليك من ربك

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: At the Farewell Pilgrimage on Arafat, the Prophet asked the assembled companions to testify that he had conveyed, fulfilled, and advised; he called God as witness. Muslim reports it from Jabir.
rows.anchor: إنكم مسؤولون عني فما أنتم قائلون

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet instructed those present to convey to those absent and to transmit even a single verse.
rows.anchor: وقد أمر أمته أن يبلغ الشاهد الغائب وقال: "بلغوا عني ولو آية"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The companions transmitted Quran and Sunnah separately; the order to erase other written material was meant to prevent its confusion with Quran, not to forbid memorizing or narrating Sunnah.
rows.anchor: ولهذا قال عليه الصلاة والسلام: "من كتب عني سوى القرآن فليمحه"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir says it is certain that all Quran delivered by the Prophet reached later generations without loss.
rows.anchor: فلهذا نعلم بالضرورة أنه لم يبق من القرآن مما أداه الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم إليهم إلا وقد بلغوه إلينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Collecting the Quran in written sheets was a major religious benefit: Abu Bakr safeguarded the sheets, Umar inherited them, Hafsa held them after Umar's death, and Uthman later took them.
rows.anchor: فكان الذي فعله الشيخان أبو بكر وعمر، رضي الله عنهما، من أكبر المصالح الدينية وأعظمها، من حفظهما كتاب الله في الصحف

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that God listens to no recitation as He listens to a prophet reciting the Quran; Muslim and al-Nasa'i transmit this route.
rows.anchor: أنه كان يقول: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

rows.speaker: صاحبه
rows.claim: An unnamed transmitter glosses the Prophet's phrase as reciting the Quran aloud.
rows.anchor: وقال صاحب له: يريد يجهر به فرد من هذا الوجه.

rows.speaker: سفيان
rows.claim: Sufyan explains the phrase as finding sufficiency in the Quran.
rows.anchor: قال سفيان: تفسيره: يستغني به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir explains the hadith as God's special attention to a prophet who recites aloud beautifully; prophets combine a fine voice with complete reverence and excellent constitution.
rows.anchor: ومعناه: أن الله ما استمع لشيء كاستماعه لقراءة نبي يجهر بقراءته ويحسنها

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha said that God's hearing encompasses all sounds; Ibn Kathir says He hears all servants but attends more closely to believers' Quran recitation, and most closely to prophets' recitation.
rows.anchor: كما قالت عائشة، رضي الله عنها: سبحان الله الذي وسع سمعه الأصوات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir prefers interpreting udhn here as listening rather than command, based on the immediate context and the sky and earth listening to God in 84:1-5.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من فسر الأذن هاهنا بالأمر، والأول أولى لقوله

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A good-chain report from Fadala ibn Ubayd compares God's listening to a man with a beautiful voice reciting aloud to a songstress listening to her singer.
rows.anchor: عن فضالة بن عبيد قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Uqba ibn Amir reports that the Prophet told Quran students to learn and acquire the Book, and the narrator was unsure whether he also said to recite it melodiously.
rows.anchor: عن عقبة بن عامر قال: خرج علينا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second route through Musa ibn Ali says without uncertainty, acquire the Quran and recite it melodiously; Ahmad and al-Nasa'i transmit both routes.
rows.anchor: من حديث موسى بن علي، عن أبيه به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A version in which the Prophet greets people reading Quran supports greeting a person who is reciting.
rows.anchor: وفي بعض ألفاظه: خرج علينا ونحن نقرأ القرآن فسلم علينا، وذكر الحديث.

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Al-Muhasir ibn Habib reports in a mursal narration: people of the Quran should not use it as a pillow, should recite it at all hours, acquire it, and reflect on it for success.
rows.anchor: عن المهاصر بن حبيب قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد
rows.claim: Abu Ubayd glosses taghannawhu as making Quran one's sufficiency instead of poverty, and iqtanuhu as acquiring it like wealth.
rows.anchor: ثم قال أبو عبيد: قوله: "تغنوه": يعني: اجعلوه غناءكم من الفقر

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Abu Ubayd transmits Fadala's report that God listens especially to a man with a beautiful Quran voice; Ibn Majah's route adds that he recites aloud and includes Maysara, Fadala's client, in the chain.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبيد: حدثني هشام بن عمار، عن يحيى بن حمزة، عن الأوزاعي، حدثني إسماعيل ابن عبيد الله بن أبي المهاجر، عن فضالة بن عبيد، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد
rows.claim: Abu Ubayd says the phrase about God granting permission means that God listens.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيد: يعني: الاستماع. وقوله في الحديث الآخر:

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: Umar used to ask Abu Musa to remind them of their Lord, after which Abu Musa recited for him.
rows.anchor: عن أبي سلمة قال: كان عمر إذا رأى أبا موسى قال: ذكرنا ربنا يا أبا موسى

rows.speaker: أبو عثمان النهدي
rows.claim: Abu Uthman al-Nahdi said Abu Musa's prayer-leading voice sounded more beautiful than any cymbal, lute, or other sound he had heard.
rows.anchor: كان أبو موسى يصلي بنا، فلو قلت: إني لم أسمع صوت صنج قط، ولا بربط قط

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha says she heard an unusually beautiful recitation from a Companion, and the Prophet went with her to listen and identified the reader as Salim, client of Abu Hudhayfa; Ibn Kathir grades the chain good.
rows.anchor: عن عائشة قالت: " أبطأت على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ليلة بعد العشاء

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet praised God for placing a reciter like Salim in his community.
rows.anchor: هذا سالم مولى أبي حذيفة، الحمد لله الذي جعل في أمتي مثل هذا

rows.speaker: جبير بن مطعم
rows.claim: Jubayr heard the Prophet recite al-Tur in the Maghrib prayer and said no one recited more beautifully; the verse about creation made him feel his heart would split.
rows.anchor: وفي الصحيحين عن جبير بن مطعم قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقرأ في المغرب بالطور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jubayr was still a polytheist when he heard this, arriving later after Badr to ransom captives; Ibn Kathir says the recitation caused his guidance.
rows.anchor: وكان جبير لما سمع هذا بعد مشركا على دين قومه، وإنما قدم في فداء الأسارى بعد بدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The best Quran recitation is rooted in a reverent heart, not merely a pleasant voice.
rows.anchor: ولهذا كان أحسن القراءة ما كان عن خشوع القلب

rows.speaker: طاوس
rows.claim: Tawus says the person with the best Quran voice is the one most fearful of God.
rows.anchor: عن ليث، عن طاوس قال: أحسن الناس صوتا بالقرآن أخشاهم لله

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: In a report through Tawus, the Prophet says the best Quran voice belongs to the person whose recitation makes a listener see that he fears God.
rows.anchor: عن ابن طاوس، عن أبيه، وعن الحسن بن مسلم، عن طاوس قال: سئل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Harith al-A'war reports that Gabriel told the Prophet his community would differ; the Quran is the refuge that saves whoever clings to it and destroys any tyrant who abandons it, and its marvels do not end.
rows.anchor: قال: ثم قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول:

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Ali reports the Prophet describing the Quran as the account of past peoples, news of the future, and judgment among people; it is the decisive word, an unbreakable rope, a straight path, and never exhausted by repetition.
rows.anchor: أما إني سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول:

rows.speaker: الترمذي
rows.claim: Al-Tirmidhi calls the report gharīb, says it is known only through Hamza al-Zayyat, and judges its chain unknown, adding that Harith's report is criticized.
rows.anchor: ثم قال: هذا حديث غريب لا نعرفه إلا من حديث حمزة الزيات، وإسناده مجهول وفي حديث الحارث مقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The third class of Israelite reports is neither confirmed nor contradicted by Islamic sources; one should neither believe nor deny it, though it may be related, and it usually has no religious benefit.
rows.anchor: والثالث: ما هو مسكوت عنه لا من هذا القبيل ولا من هذا القبيل، فلا نؤمن به ولا نكذبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Examples include the Cave Companions' names, dog's color and number, the tree of Moses' staff, Abraham's birds, the cow part used in the murder, and the tree from which God spoke to Moses; Quranic silence leaves these details without useful consequence.
rows.anchor: كما يذكرون في مثل هذا أسماء أصحاب الكهف، ولون كلبهم، وعدتهم، وعصا موسى من أي الشجر كانت؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In 18:22, Ibn Kathir says the Quran weakens the claims of three or five sleepers and leaves the claim of seven unchallenged, showing it is correct; it teaches people not to argue beyond what is useful or ask the People of the Book.
rows.anchor: فقد اشتملت هذه الآية الكريمة على الأدب في هذا المقام وتعليم ما ينبغي في مثل هذا، فإنه تعالى أخبر عنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran says that only a few know the sleepers' number and directs the Prophet to answer that God knows it, since seeking the detail has no value.
rows.anchor: فإنه ما يعلم بذلك إلا قليل من الناس، ممن أطلعه الله عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The best way to report disagreement is to include all views, identify the sound one, reject false ones, and state what practical benefit the disagreement has.
rows.anchor: فهذا أحسن ما يكون في حكاية الخلاف: أن تستوعب الأقوال في ذلك المقام، وأن تنبه على الصحيح منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report of disagreement is incomplete if it omits views or gives them without identifying the correct one, since the omitted view may be right and uncorrected error misleads.
rows.anchor: فأما من حكى خلافا في مسألة ولم يستوعب أقوال الناس فيها فهو ناقص، إذ قد يكون الصواب في الذي تركه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Someone who knowingly endorses a false view has deliberately lied; someone who does so unknowingly has erred.
rows.anchor: فإن صحح غير الصحيح عامدا فقد تعمد الكذب، أو جاهلا فقد أخطأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inventing disagreements about useless matters or multiplying wordings that reduce to one or two positions wastes time and is like wearing two garments of falsehood.
rows.anchor: وكذلك من نصب الخلاف فيما لا فائدة تحته، أو حكى أقوالا متعددة لفظا ويرجع حاصلها إلى قول أو قولين معنى
